title: The Missing Ledger
premise: Insurance investigator Gideon Reyes has spent years solving murders the police mislabeled as accidents, using his photographic memory to notice what others miss while keeping his own name out of every file. When a drowned accountant is found wearing clothes stolen from Gideon's closet, he realizes someone is framing him for a death connected to the Halvorsen warehouse fire—a case closed fifteen years ago that killed his father and haunts the edges of his memory. As the statute of limitations expires in nine days, Gideon must reconstruct the missing ledger that proves the fire was arson-for-hire, racing a killer who knows his mind better than anyone should. In the end, Gideon chooses justice over invisibility, testifying to expose the fire's architect—his own mentor—even as it costs him the anonymous life he built.
about_author: Casper Fairweather is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent eleven years reading other people's disasters before turning them into fiction. He writes from a coastal town where fog is frequent and bodies are, thankfully, rare.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Called to assess a drowning claim, Gideon recognizes the victim's outfit instantly—it was stolen from his own closet days earlier. His photographic memory catalogues every detail at the scene: staged wine glasses, a forged suicide note in handwriting mimicking his own. The emotional beat is cold dread; the invisible man has been made visible, and the frame is personal.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Ash
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, with flashback interludes. Digging into the victim's finances, Gideon finds payments tracing back to the Halvorsen warehouse fire—the blaze that killed his father and that he witnessed as a child but can't fully retrieve from memory. His old mentor, retired investigator Marcus Vane, offers help. The beat is grief resurfacing; the case everyone swore was closed was buried deliberately.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Ghost
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Reconstructing the burned ledger from fragments—the victim's hidden copies, a bank microfiche, his own fractured childhood recollection—Gideon proves the fire was arson-for-insurance, ordered by someone inside the investigation itself. When a second witness dies and police name Gideon a suspect, he realizes only Marcus knew his methods well enough to frame him. The beat is betrayal sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Memory Owes
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. On the statute's final day, Gideon lures Marcus into confessing by reciting the ledger aloud—every figure, every date—forcing the old man to confront that his protégé's perfect memory has already convicted him. Marcus is arrested; the frame collapses. Gideon testifies publicly, ending his anonymity. The beat is bittersweet release: justice costs him his hiding place, and he accepts the price.
